correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the coordinatewise Rayleigh/centred-embedding inequality lambda_2 S <= B for arbitrary nonsymmetric conductances. For q>=p, placing p vertices at the origin and q as a zero-sum unit polygon gives S=q with the added edge length zero; for p>q and p>=4 the compensated polygon construction yields S=p, again with added edge length zero. Uniform Kpq weights achieve B/max(p,q). For (p,q)=(3,2), the specified 2D embedding has S=V=(11+2sqrt(3))/5; the unscaled weights a=(3+2/sqrt(3))/10, b=(4+sqrt(3))/10, c=(1-1/sqrt(3))/5 total V and have lambda_2=1. Strict gain over B/3 forces all optimal added-edge weights positive. Direct independent weighted spectral calculations confirmed 123 bounded cases; infinite ranges follow from the algebraic constructions and exact spectra.

value.rationale: A precise universal test for whether one new edge is worth assigning any positive part of a fixed conductance budget in a natural graph family, with a unique exceptional graph and exact optimum; useful as a network design and algebraic-connectivity benchmark.

final_claim: For all p,q>=2 and B>0, the maximum weighted Laplacian spectral gap of K_{p,q} plus an edge inside the p-part is B/max(p,q), except (p,q)=(3,2), when it is 5B/(11+2sqrt(3)). Every optimizer uses zero added-edge conductance outside the exception, and positive added-edge conductance in the exception.
limitations: Only p,q>=2, one intra-part edge, continuous-time spectral gap and uniform per-edge budget cost; no uniqueness of full optimizer, no heterogeneous costs or discrete-time SLEM.
